pages.summary: The public properties of an object or class, and its methods.
body: Without an output, they list the names under a heading; with one, they return them as a column cell. Either takes an object or a class name. Only what is public shows: private properties and methods stay hidden.

examples.title: A class of your own
examples.intro: The class is written to its file here so that the example runs on its own.
examples.code:
lines = {
    'classdef Account < handle'
    '    properties'
    '        Owner = '''''
    '        Balance = 0'
    '    end'
    '    properties (Access = private)'
    '        Log = {}'
    '    end'
    '    methods'
    '        function deposit(a, x)'
    '            a.Balance = a.Balance + x;'
    '            a.Log{end + 1} = x;'
    '        end'
    '        function withdraw(a, x)'
    '            a.Balance = a.Balance - x;'
    '        end'
    '    end'
    'end'};
fid = fopen('Account.m', 'w');
fprintf(fid, '%s\n', lines{:});
fclose(fid);
properties('Account')
m = methods('Account');
m(ismember(m, {'deposit', 'withdraw'}))'
examples.output:
Properties for class Account:

    Owner
    Balance

ans = 

  1×2 cell array

    {'deposit'}    {'withdraw'}

pages.summary: Tests on objects: has it a method of a name, a property of a name, and is it an object of a class at all.
body: `isobject` is true for objects of classes (your own, maps, exceptions), and false for numbers, text, structs and cells, which are values of built-in types.

examples.title: A map, and some values that are not objects
examples.code:
k = containers.Map({'a', 'b'}, {1, 2});
[ismethod(k, 'keys') ismethod(k, 'sort') isprop(k, 'Count')]
[isobject(k) isobject(MException('my:id', 'text'))]
[isobject(5) isobject('text') isobject(struct('a', 1)) isobject({1})]
examples.output:
ans =

  1×3 logical array

   1   0   1

ans =

  1×2 logical array

   1   1

ans =

  1×4 logical array

   0   0   0   0

pages.summary: True for handle objects that have not been deleted.
body: Deleting a handle object (a figure closed, `delete(h)`) leaves the variables holding it pointing at nothing; `isvalid` tells them apart, element by element for an array of handles.
syntax: For each handle, whether it is still there.

examples.title: Before and after
examples.output:
ans =

  1×2 logical array

   1   1

ans =

  1×3 logical array

   0   1   0

pages.summary: Events of handle objects: raised by notify, heard by listeners.
body: A handle class lists its events in an `events` block, and its methods raise them with `notify(obj, 'EventName')`. `addlistener` attaches a callback, which is given the object and the event data (`Source`, `EventName`, and any fields given to `notify`); its listener's `Enabled` turns it off and on, and `delete(L)` removes it. `listener` makes one too. `events` lists a class's events; every handle class also has `ObjectBeingDestroyed`, raised by `delete`.

examples.title: A tank that warns when it overflows
examples.code:
lines = {
    'classdef Tank < handle'
    '    properties'
    '        Level = 0'
    '    end'
    '    events'
    '        Overflow'
    '    end'
    '    methods'
    '        function fill(t, amount)'
    '            t.Level = t.Level + amount;'
    '            if t.Level > 100'
    '                notify(t, ''Overflow'');'
    '            end'
    '        end'
    '    end'
    'end'};
fid = fopen('Tank.m', 'w');
fprintf(fid, '%s\n', lines{:});
fclose(fid);
t = Tank;
L = addlistener(t, 'Overflow', @(src, evt) fprintf('%s at level %g\n', evt.EventName, src.Level));
fill(t, 60)
fill(t, 60)
L.Enabled = false;
fill(t, 10)
events(t)
examples.output:
Overflow at level 120

Events for class Tank:

    Overflow
    ObjectBeingDestroyed

pages.summary: The description of a class: its name, properties, methods, events and superclasses.
body: `metaclass(obj)`, `?ClassName` and `meta.class.fromName('ClassName')` give a `meta.class` object. Its lists describe the class, inherited parts included: `PropertyList` (each with `Name`, `GetAccess`, `SetAccess`, `Dependent`, `Constant`, `DefaultValue`, ...), `MethodList` (`Name`, `Access`, `Static`, ...), `EventList` and `SuperclassList`. `?A < ?B` is true when class A derives from B.
syntax: The class of an object; `?ClassName` gives a class by its name.

pages.summary: A copy of a handle object, for classes that derive from matlab.mixin.Copyable (and of a datastore).
body: Assigning a handle object to another variable shares it; `copy` makes a second object with the same property values. The copy is shallow: handles held in its properties are shared, not copied, unless the class overrides `copyElement` (starting from `copyElement@matlab.mixin.Copyable(obj)`); properties marked `NonCopyable` get their defaults.

examples.title: Shared, and copied

pages.summary: What a class's calls to its superclass become: obj@Super(args) in a constructor and method@Super(obj, args) in a method.
body: In a subclass's constructor, `obj = obj@Super(args)` (or the call alone, `obj@Super(args);`) runs the superclass's constructor on the object being made; in a method, `method@Super(obj, args)` runs the superclass's version of a method the subclass overrides. PyLAB writes these as calls to `plabSuperCall` when it reads the class; the function is not called by hand, and the `@` forms are what is written in a class.

examples.title: A constructor and a method that build on the superclass's
examples.code:
lines = {
    'classdef Animal'
    '    properties'
    '        Name'
    '    end'
    '    methods'
    '        function a = Animal(name)'
    '            a.Name = name;'
    '        end'
    '        function s = describe(a)'
    '            s = [''an animal called '' a.Name];'
    '        end'
    '    end'
    'end'};
fid = fopen('Animal.m', 'w');
fprintf(fid, '%s\n', lines{:});
fclose(fid);
lines = {
    'classdef Dog < Animal'
    '    properties'
    '        Breed'
    '    end'
    '    methods'
    '        function d = Dog(name, breed)'
    '            d@Animal(name);'
    '            d.Breed = breed;'
    '        end'
    '        function s = describe(d)'
    '            s = [describe@Animal(d) '', a '' d.Breed];'
    '        end'
    '    end'
    'end'};
fid = fopen('Dog.m', 'w');
fprintf(fid, '%s\n', lines{:});
fclose(fid);
d = Dog('Rex', 'collie');
describe(d)
isa(d, 'Animal')
examples.output:
ans =

    'an animal called Rex, a collie'

ans =

  logical

   1
